This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. Russia and Ukraine exchanged attacks overnight.
Ukraine says at least nine are dead there with one person killed in Russia. The fighting came
despite a new push by the Trump administration to find an end to the conflict, as NPR's Charles
Mains reports. White House envoy Steve Whitcoff held talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin
in St. Petersburg on Wednesday, a meeting that saw Whitcoff praise the Kremlin leader as a
humanitarian for releasing a wrongfully detained American, and Putin agreed to rejoin U.S. mediated
talks with Ukraine. Yet just hours later, Russia fired a barrage of missiles on Ukraine's capital
Kiev and Ukraine countered with drone attacks on Moscow. Russia's defense ministry said it had
targeted factories involved in the production of rockets and drones. Yet Ukrainian President
Vladimir Zelensky accused Russia of hitting civilian infrastructure, a sign he added that
despite Whitcoff's praise for the Kremlin leader, Russia's position hadn't changed.
Charles Mains, NPR News, Moscow. A federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to halt
investigations in nine states into whether non-citizens are registered to vote. The judge says
the effort is relying on data that's full of errors and that it's intimidating groups doing
voter assistance efforts, but she put the rolling on hold until tomorrow to give the administration
a chance to appeal. The Trump administration says it has no plans to investigate people it believes
are U.S. citizens. The Department of Justice has indicted a prominent Virginia Democrat on
charges including racketeering, money laundering, and conspiracy to distribute marijuana. From
VPM News, Jad Khalil reports. It made the FBI rated a cannabis dispensary connected to the senior
Democrat in the Virginia Senate, Eloise Lucas. The indictment alleges she and others used their
businesses to sell illegal marijuana. It also alleges she used her position to enrich herself
by working to legalize marijuana. The 82-year-old Lucas, who is black and a frequent critic of
Republicans, said in a statement she grew up under Jim Crow and has "seen what happens when
people in power try to silence those who stand up to them." Attorney General Todd Blanche rejected
allegations that politics influenced the investigation, saying the probe into Lucas
began before the Trump administration took office. For NPR News, I'm Jad Khalil in Richmond, Virginia.
A sell-off in AI stocks like Meta pummeled stock markets today, sending the tech-heavy Nasdaq down
more than 2 percent, NPR's Rafael Naum reports. It's becoming a well-known sequence. AI stocks
rally for a while amid hopes about game-changing technology, only to then suffer big sell-offs as
investors get skittish about how much money is being spent across the sector. The latest example
is Meta. Its shares plunged after the company said it would need to continue increasing spending on
AI, including unbuilding data centers. Other AI stocks are also down sharply, including Nvidia.
Rafael Naum, NPR News. The S&P 500 fell more than 1 percent for its worst day since July. This is NPR.
The International Criminal Court has won the European Union's top human rights honor,
the Sakharov Prize. The award comes just days after the Trump administration announced sweeping
new sanctions on the ICC. The sanctions are part of a campaign to dismantle the tribunal over
investigations into certain conduct by the United States and its allies, including Israel.
The economy continues to be a major source of stress for most Americans, with nearly 8 in 10
reporting that the cost of living is the biggest stressor in their lives. That's according to a new
survey. As NPR's Ritu Chatterjee reports, a majority of respondents say that stress has become
their new normal. Financial pressures and concerns about the future of the country remain on top of
people's minds, according to the latest annual Stress in America survey by the American Psychological
Association, or the APA. But six in 10 adults also reported health care as a big source of stress.
Psychologist Vail Wright is senior director of health care innovation at the APA.
More than a third of young adults, so aged 18 to 29. So they put their future on hold
this year as a result of their stress. And that to me is very concerning.
Nearly half of survey respondents also reported that stress is keeping them
from participating in social activities. Ritu Chatterjee, NPR News.
A city in South Korea is again trying to free a huge shark from a narrow canal.
Workers in Busan had herded the shark, nicknamed Bukangi, out of the canal yesterday after
weeks of trial and error. But Bukangi swam beneath a barrier net and re-entered the waterway today.
I'm Rylan Barton, and from Washington, this is NPR News.
